solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Woman to run off after writer

indicators.note: the running-off piece comes after the writer, so it is placed second

parts.note: a pen is the writing implement, a common crossword stand-in for writer
to run off with a lover to marry is to elope

explanation.surface: A woman runs away with a novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope is a female given name, famously the faithful wife of Odysseus.

clue.text: The heart's gone out of well-liked part of London

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, and here that centre has been removed

parts.note: someone well-liked is popular

explanation.surface: A once-loved London district has lost its spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The heart's gone out of' removes U, the middle letter of the seven-letter POPULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplar is a district in the East End of London, in the borough of Tower Hamlets.

clue.text: No regional accent heard from someone in our area?

indicators.note: the clue says these words are listened to, so their sound gives the entry

parts.note: no is NAY, and a burr is a regional accent with a rolled R, as in the West Country

explanation.surface: Someone local who speaks without a trace of any regional accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, NAY + BURR gives the sound of the entry; a burr is a rough, rolled R typical of Scottish or West Country speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour is a person living nearby, in the same street or locality.

clue.text: Foolish candidates ultimately lose deposit

indicators.note: foolish suggests a muddled state, so the letters of lose are scrambled
ultimately points to the final letter of candidates

explanation.surface: Silly election candidates forfeit their deposits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolish' rearranges LOSE to LOES; 'ultimately' adds S, the last letter of candidates. In British elections a candidate who polls too few votes loses a cash deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: Loess is a fine windblown sediment, a geological deposit of silt.

clue.text: Extending hospitality? That could get you shot!

definitions.text: Extending hospitality? That could get you shot!

parts.words: Extending hospitality? That could get you shot!
parts.note: the phrase means entertaining guests; the joke is that the one doing it may well be handed a shot of spirits, or shot at like a target in a game

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is the plain meaning; the joke treats 'playing' as a risky game in which the one doing it is exposed to a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To be acting as the giver of a party or welcome is to be receiving and entertaining guests.

clue.text: Non-workers led astray in the grip of wicked sir

indicators.note: one set of letters is held inside the other, as if gripped
wicked here hints at the letters of sir being twisted out of shape
led astray suggests going off course, so these three letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lazy people are corrupted by an evil knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' looks like a description of the knight but is an anagram signal, as is 'astray'; 'in the grip of' puts one jumble (DLE) inside the other (IRS).
explanation.definitionFit: Idlers are lazy people who avoid work, hence non-workers.

clue.text: Sunday's party skirt above the knee term "short"

parts.note: a do is a party
a miniskirt, a mini, ends above the knee

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: to term something is to call it by a name

explanation.surface: A Sunday party with a short skirt and a brief remark about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims CALL to CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominical means relating to Sunday as the Lord's Day, from Latin dominicus, of the Lord.

clue.text: Lords offering bits of wisdom, but not quietly

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the quietly letter from the word

parts.note: pearls of wisdom are wise sayings
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Peers dispense their wisdom loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes P (piano, quietly) from PEARLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls are noblemen, members of the peerage, so lords.

clue.text: Tread is wobbly with age finally creeping in? In younger days one was this!

definitions.text: Tread is wobbly with age finally creeping in? In younger days one was this!

indicators.note: the age letter slips inside the rearranged letters
wobbly suggests unsteady letters, so tread and is are rearranged
finally points to the last letter of age

explanation.surface: An old person's step has grown shaky; once they walked more firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbly' turns TREADIS into STEADIR; 'creeping in' slips in E, the last letter of age, giving the whole word. The whole clue is the definition: once, when young, one was firmer on one's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: In youth a person's gait was firmer and less shaky, the comparative of steady.

clue.text: Proper English girl before Man came along?

parts.note: prim means primly proper
Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie

explanation.surface: A prim English girl who predates humanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Primeval means of the earliest ages of the world, before human beings existed.

clue.text: It's fine in the morning before a hint of cloud comes in

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, in the morning

indicators.note: the hint letter enters the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A sunny morning before a little cloud arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hint of' takes C from cloud; 'comes in' puts it inside ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To amerce is to punish with a fine, an old legal verb.

clue.text: In the afternoon Pip's abandoned girl

indicators.note: abandoned says that the Pip part is dropped

parts.note: p.m. in the old signallers' alphabet was spoken as pip emma
Pip was the signallers' word for the letter P

explanation.surface: A girl left behind by Pip one afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: In the old military signalling alphabet P was Pip and M was Emma, so p.m. was PIP EMMA; 'abandoned' drops PIP. Pip also suggests the hero of Great Expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a female name, as in Jane Austen's heroine.

clue.text: Female with outer oomph about to become a trophy

indicators.note: the oomph letters sit on the outside, around the female
about signals that the letters are turned round

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is oomph
she is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A sexy woman becomes a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: SA (sex appeal) is a crossword convention for oomph. The Ashes is the cricket trophy contested between England and Australia, named for a mock obituary of English cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashes, a tiny urn, is the prize in England-Australia Test cricket series.

clue.text: I am maiden with fancy undies given protection from something nasty?

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: fancy suggests elaborate rearrangement of the letters of undies

explanation.surface: A girl in frilly underwear protected from something unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges UNDIES to UNISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being vaccinated gives protection from a disease, the something nasty.

clue.text: Curved pin in vessel, say

parts.note: a bowl is a vessel
e.g., for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A bent pin inside some kind of container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pin' is slang for leg, not a sewing pin.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowleg is a leg bowed outwards, and pins are legs in slang.

clue.text: Letters descend on Westminster house

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on the second

parts.note: to land is to come down
the House of Lords is one of the two houses of Parliament at Westminster

explanation.surface: Post arrives at the Houses of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' are not mail but people who let property.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlords let out property to tenants, so they are those who let.

clue.text: Cunning this writer has used to produce document

parts.note: arch means sly or cunning
the setter saying I have gives I've

explanation.surface: The author confesses to slyness in producing a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a stored record or collection of documents, so a document.

clue.text: Liaison to break up — loneliness resulting

indicators.note: breaking up shatters the letters of liaison and to into a new order

explanation.surface: A love affair ends, leaving someone lonely.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolation is being cut off from others, a state of solitude.

clue.text: Platform providing timeless facts about group of followers

indicators.note: about signals the shortened word is turned backwards
timeless means the time letter, T, is removed

parts.note: a fold is a flock or congregation, a group of believers

explanation.surface: A political platform giving facts free of timing about a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' takes T from FACTS to give FACS; 'about' turns it to SCAF.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised platform, for builders or for an execution.

clue.text: My home — this is demolished in Greek city

parts.note: cor! is an exclamation like my!
in means at home

indicators.note: demolished means is is knocked out of this

explanation.surface: My house has been knocked down in a Greek city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' removes IS from THIS, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth is an ancient city of Greece on the isthmus near Athens.

clue.text: See 4
Expression of pain? First take tablet — it may help you sleep

indicators.note: first says the tablet piece goes at the front

parts.note: a pill is a tablet
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Someone in pain is advised to take a tablet to help them sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow is a cushion for the head in bed, an aid to slumber.

clue.text: Indication of lust with one about to show great desire

parts.note: to make a pass at someone shows sexual interest
I is the Roman numeral one
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A sign of lust, coupled with one about to reveal a strong want.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion is intense desire or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Wild animal sailor brought over a lake

indicators.note: in a down clue the sailor sits over the rest

parts.note: Jack, Jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor brought a wild beast across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackal is a wild dog of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Winners and losers ultimately

parts.note: in a competition's last match both sides, the eventual winner and loser, are those who reached the deciding round

explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' looks like a selection signal for last letters, but the clue is a definition: those in the final become winner and loser.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitors who reach the last round of a contest, one of whom wins and one loses.

clue.text: Records revolutionary attack

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning right round, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: to set on someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: Documents of a rebel assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns SET ON backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are written records or jottings.

clue.text: Plant, one found in particular wood

indicators.note: the single letter is found inside the wood

parts.note: lana is a specific timber, the hard wood of the South American genipap tree
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A plant found in a certain wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests.

clue.text: Material left on land cut off by water

indicators.note: in a down clue the left letter sits on top

parts.note: an isle is land surrounded by water

explanation.surface: Fabric left on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine smooth cotton thread used for stockings.

clue.text: Protest in court unusual — last thing royalty needs

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of court are put in an odd order
the last thing in royalty is its final letter

explanation.surface: An unusual protest in court is the last thing royals want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges COURT to OUTCR; 'last thing' adds Y from royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a loud public protest.

clue.text: GB is getting awkward moment — there's a nasty threat

indicators.note: getting awkward suggests letters falling into a clumsy new order

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in just a tick

explanation.surface: Britain faces an awkward moment amid a nasty threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting awkward' rearranges GBIS to BIGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A big stick is a threat of force, from Roosevelt's speak softly and carry one.

clue.text: Order issued — our pits were destined to fall into this

definitions.text: our pits were destined to fall into this

indicators.note: order means put in order, so the letters of issued are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A government order meant Britain's coal mines would be closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' rearranges ISSUED. The surface recalls the closure of British coal mines in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Disuse is the state of no longer being used, as abandoned mines are.

clue.text: It's hellish inside — fright's beginning, not ending

indicators.note: not says that the ending of fright's is replaced by its beginning

parts.note: internal means inside

indicators.note: the beginning of fright's is its first letter

explanation.surface: It is hellish indoors, with fear setting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ending' means swap out T (the ending of fright) from INTERNAL and put F (its beginning) in, under 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal means of hell, from Latin infernus, the underworld.
